hypotheses.claim: A minimal HTTP+SQLite CRUD vertical slice can be realized without changing ClayCode core semantics if HTTP and database operations are exposed through typed adapters over existing state/effect/outcome/rollback/resource concepts.
support: EXP-SPAWN-F1-HTTPDB-001: local deterministic narrow lowering witness passed 17/17 tests
WASI HTTP demonstrates a typed host-interface pattern for HTTP
HTTP semantics are separable from wire/version details
hypotheses.falsifier: Production ClayCode parser/type/effect/lowering on the current G9 stack cannot express or enforce the slice without an untyped semantic escape hatch or a new core primitive.

hypotheses.claim: Transaction atomicity can initially live in a typed DB adapter/runtime contract rather than new ClayCode surface syntax, provided transaction resource identity, commit/rollback outcome, partial-effect state and retry semantics are explicit and receipted.
support: Injected create/update/delete failures rolled back in the local SQLite witness
hypotheses.falsifier: A real ClayCode lowering cannot preserve transaction atomicity/replay identity with adapter-level contracts, or mixed/partial commit cannot be represented truthfully.

hypotheses.claim: HTTP method/path/status/body details belong primarily in a typed standard-library/FFI contract, not the ClayCode core language.
support: RFC 9110 separates HTTP semantics from version-specific messaging syntax
WASI HTTP exposes HTTP through typed component interfaces
hypotheses.falsifier: A real ClayCode application requires core-language semantics to distinguish HTTP behavior that cannot be encoded by ordinary typed values/effects/resources/results.

counterhypotheses.claim: Current G9 generic effect/rollback semantics are too weak for database transaction closure, so a first-class transaction semantic primitive is required.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Compile and execute the same slice with production ClayCode; inspect whether atomicity, rollback and partial-effect semantics require an escape hatch.

counterhypotheses.claim: The proxy succeeds only because Python/SQLite hide semantics that ClayCode must itself model; production lowering will expose missing ownership/lifetime/error/transaction rules.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Run the production backend with mutation/fault injection and compare semantic receipts against the reference witness.
